title: 14 Best AI App Builders for Turning AI-Generated Prototypes Into Real Apps in 2027

body_markdown:
Prototypes often die the moment they reach developers. Every interaction tested, every screen refined, gets rebuilt from scratch because demo code was never meant for production. That gap between "it works in the demo" and "it works for real users" can create additional development work, delays, and costs. According to the Stack Overflow survey,[65.9% of 17,464 respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) reported using AI coding assistants or coding agents at work in 2026.


Looking toward 2027, that workflow is increasingly optional. AI app builders have evolved from tools that generate mockups to platforms that deploy working applications with[managed backend infrastructure](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-backend-platforms) , databases, authentication, and hosting. The question is no longer whether AI can build apps. The question is which tools bridge the prototype-to-production gap without forcing teams to start over.


The stakes are higher than convenience. Georgia Tech researchers[identified 74 confirmed cases](https://www.cc.gatech.edu/news/bad-vibes-ai-generated-code-vulnerable-researchers-warn) linked to AI-generated code in their April 2026 findings, highlighting why security review matters when moving AI-built applications into production. As AI adoption grows, choosing a platform that supports testing, reliable infrastructure, and ongoing development becomes increasingly important.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Full-stack infrastructure matters:** Floot provides[managed backend infrastructure](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-databases) , including Postgres databases, authentication, file storage, and hosting, helping builders move beyond prototypes without configuring separate services.
- **Mobile deployment approaches differ:** Floot packages web apps in installable iOS and Android shells without requiring a Mac or Xcode. Its[mobile publishing guide](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-mobile-apps) explains build allowances, developer accounts, and app-store requirements.
- **Code ownership enables flexibility:** Floot users own their project code, app data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database exports are available across plans, while[full code downloads](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) require a paid subscription.
- **Connector-based development reduces duplicate AI billing:** Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) works with supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Standard connector operations use the connected assistant's AI subscription rather than separate Floot AI build credits.
- **Floot is free to start:** Floot provides daily building-action allowances and managed hosting, with paid plans offering additional capacity. Its[current pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) separate building actions, optional AI credits, hosting allowances, and mobile builds.


## **What to Look for in an AI App Builder**


Turning a prototype into a production app requires more than code generation. Teams should evaluate platforms based on infrastructure, portability, deployment options, and their ability to support applications beyond the initial demonstration.


- **Production Readiness:** Can the generated code handle real user traffic, or does it need additional development? Platforms that include managed databases, authentication, and hosting can provide more direct paths to production than those outputting frontend code alone. Security testing and deployment reviews remain necessary.
- **Code Ownership and Portability:** GitHub sync, ZIP export, and the ability to self-host matter when outgrowing a platform or bringing in developers later. Some platforms offer code export on all plans, while others restrict it to paid tiers. Ownership does not necessarily mean an application can run elsewhere without modification.
- **Mobile Deployment Path:** Native mobile apps require different approaches. Some builders generate Flutter or React Native code, while others wrap web apps in native shells. The distinction affects App Store approval, performance, and long-term maintenance. Users should also verify developer-account and publishing requirements.
- **Backend Infrastructure:** A working app needs[database and authentication](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-built-in-databases) , backend logic, storage, and reliable deployment. Evaluate whether the platform provides these services directly or requires configuration of third-party providers, particularly when building apps that store customer information.
- **AI Integration Model:** Some platforms use their own AI agents with separate credit systems. Others connect to external AI assistants through protocols like MCP. The billing, permissions, and available development capabilities differ, so teams should evaluate both AI usage costs and infrastructure requirements.


The prices below are in USD and reflect published pricing checked on November 23, 2026, for readers planning projects in 2027. Unless otherwise noted, prices refer to standard monthly billing. Annual discounts, regional taxes, and usage charges may differ.


## **1. Floot**


Floot is a[full-stack app-building platform](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations.


Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development. Available building capabilities depend on the AI client's connector permissions and supported tools.


### **Primary Focus**


Floot addresses the prototype-to-production gap by providing managed backend infrastructure, mobile app publishing, and code ownership while working as a connector to existing AI assistants rather than requiring a separate AI subscription.


Teams already paying for Claude or ChatGPT can build full-stack applications through supported configurations, with Floot handling the infrastructure layer. The platform is particularly suited to non-technical founders, operators, and business owners who need applications with user accounts and saved data.


### **Why Floot Leads**


Floot's MCP connector lets teams build through supported AI assistants while using managed infrastructure for application development and publishing. Rather than replacing tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, Floot works alongside them by supplying the services their applications need to run.


Its key capabilities include:


- **MCP-based development:** Supported assistants can manage project files, database operations, testing, and deployment through[Floot's connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , subject to client permissions. Standard connector operations use building actions rather than Floot AI credits.
- **Managed backend services:** Floot provides[Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication with supported OAuth providers, file storage, CDN-backed assets, and serverless backend endpoints without requiring separate infrastructure configuration.
- **Mobile app publishing:** Floot packages web apps in installable iOS and Android shells. Its[mobile development workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) handles cloud-based builds without requiring a Mac, Xcode, or Android Studio.
- **Code ownership and portability:** Users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database exports are available to all users, while[project ZIP downloads](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) and self-hosting options are available through paid plans.
- **Flexible billing:** Floot separates building actions, AI credits, and hosting charges. Image generation, its optional in-app AI agent, and AI features inside published applications may consume Floot credits.


This combination allows teams to work within familiar AI assistants while Floot manages application infrastructure, deployment, and ongoing hosting.


### **Flexible Pricing and Seamless App Deployment**


Floot is free to start. Its[pricing structure](https://floot.com/en/pricing) includes three plans:


- **Free:** $0/month, 100 building actions per day, 3,000 starter AI credits, a one-time $3 hosting allowance, and 2 mobile builds per month.
- **Pro:** $25/month, 1,000 building actions per day, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and 12 mobile builds per month.
- **Power:** $100/month, 5,000 building actions per day, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25 monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds.


### **Easy Mobile App Building and Publishing**


Building actions are metered separately from AI credits. Failed actions do not count, and action allowances reset daily. The Free plan's hosting credit is a one-time starter allowance rather than a recurring monthly amount. Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-based and draws on prepaid credit.


Mobile builds run on Floot's infrastructure without requiring local development tools. Publishing requires the user's own Apple or Google developer account. Connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, and store approval remains subject to Apple and Google's review processes.


Floot is backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2025 batch) and serves[non-technical builders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) using conversational app development. Teams already paying for compatible AI assistants can evaluate whether Floot's managed infrastructure meets their production deployment needs.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable, formerly GPT Engineer, is a full-stack AI app builder that generates working web applications from natural language prompts. It has become a prominent platform in this category.


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable generates TanStack Start applications with server-side rendering for new projects. Users describe what they want to build, and the platform creates the frontend, backend integration, and deployment configuration.


The result is a working application rather than a static mockup. Existing projects may retain older React and Vite architectures, while newer projects use TanStack Start for integrated frontend and backend functionality.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable provides GitHub synchronization, managed hosting, database integrations, and visual development capabilities. These features suit teams that want to generate applications through prompts while retaining access to their project code.


Teams comparing development workflows can also review Floot's[Lovable alternatives guide](https://floot.com/blog/lovable-mcp-alternatives) , which examines different approaches to AI-assisted app building and billing.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Two-way GitHub sync on all plans, including Free
- Supabase backend integration for database and authentication
- Publishing through Lovable's managed hosting infrastructure, with Cloudflare Workers supporting newer TanStack Start projects
- Figma-to-code import for design handoffs
- React and Vite codebases for older projects


### **Considerations**


Lovable works primarily with web applications. Teams needing native mobile apps should check whether the web-first output meets their App Store requirements.


Pricing starts at $25/month for the Pro plan, with AI building usage governed by credit allowances.


## **3. Replit**


Replit is a cloud IDE with an AI Agent that builds, tests, fixes, and deploys applications with minimal supervision. It supports both web and mobile development through Expo integration.


### **Primary Focus**


Replit provides a full development environment in the browser. Its AI Agent can create backend logic, frontend interfaces, and database schemas, then deploy the result to Replit's infrastructure.


This full-stack approach reduces the handoff between prototype and production. It also gives technical teams direct access to development tools while supporting AI-assisted generation and debugging.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit offers built-in PostgreSQL databases, ZIP downloads and GitHub synchronization for code portability, Expo support for mobile app builds, autoscaling deployment infrastructure, and collaborative editing.


Teams evaluating other development workflows can explore[Replit alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/replit-alternatives) , particularly when comparing managed infrastructure, AI usage models, and deployment capabilities.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Built-in PostgreSQL database
- ZIP download and GitHub sync for code portability
- Expo support for mobile app builds
- Autoscaling deployment infrastructure
- Collaborative editing for teams


### **Considerations**


Replit is more technical than some alternatives. The learning curve can be steeper, but the development environment provides greater access to project configuration and code.


Pricing starts at $20/month for Core and $100/month for Pro under standard monthly billing. Pro supports up to 15 collaborators.


## **4. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new, built by StackBlitz, uses WebContainer technology to run frontend and backend code directly in the browser. It generates full-stack applications from single prompts.


### **Primary Focus**


The WebContainer approach means developers can prototype directly in the browser without local setup. Bolt.new supports Next.js, React, Tailwind, and Expo for mobile development.


Its browser-based environment allows teams to generate interfaces, test application behavior, and refine projects through AI-assisted conversations before deployment.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new provides prompt-based project generation, GitHub integration, deployable previews, database services through Bolt Cloud, and support for multiple frontend frameworks.


Teams considering different infrastructure and billing models can review Floot's[Bolt.new alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/bolt-new-alternatives) guide.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- One-prompt project generation with deployable code
- GitHub integration with shareable previews
- Database and backend services through Bolt Cloud
- Support for multiple frameworks, including Expo
- Team collaboration features


### **Considerations**


Bolt.new emphasizes fast iteration through a browser-based development environment. Teams needing extensive backend logic should evaluate whether the generated architecture and available cloud services meet their production requirements.


Pricing starts at $25/month for Pro, with AI usage subject to token allowances.


## **5. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is Vercel's AI app builder for generating React and Next.js applications. It supports frontend development as well as full-stack features, including backend endpoints and database integrations.


### **Primary Focus**


v0 generates Next.js applications with React, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui components. The output is designed for Vercel's deployment platform, creating a direct path from generation to production.


The platform is particularly relevant to teams that already use the React and Next.js ecosystem or want to generate application interfaces and integrate them into existing development workflows.


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 provides GitHub integration and Vercel deployment, Design Mode for visual editing, Figma imports on eligible paid plans, and a free tier with daily message allowances.


These features suit teams working with modern React applications that need AI-assisted interface generation and deployment through Vercel's infrastructure.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- GitHub integration and Vercel deployment
- Design Mode for visual editing
- Figma imports on eligible paid plans
- React and Next.js component generation
- Free tier with a 7-message daily limit


### **Considerations**


v0 supports full-stack development, but teams should evaluate its database integrations, authentication setup, and deployment configuration for their production requirements.


The Plus plan starts at $30/user/month, with additional Business and Enterprise options.


## **6. Cursor**


Cursor is an AI-native code editor that understands entire codebases for context-aware suggestions. It supports codebase-aware editing and AI-assisted development workflows.


### **Primary Focus**


Cursor can work with existing repositories or help create new projects. This makes it useful for teams extending AI-built prototypes with complex business logic or integrating generated code into larger systems.


Its development workflow remains centered on a code editor, making it particularly relevant to technical users who want AI assistance while retaining direct control over implementation.


### **Organizational Fit**


Cursor offers codebase-wide understanding, inline AI editing, Git integration, support for multiple programming languages, and a familiar VS Code-like development environment.


Cursor also works alongside Floot through the[Floot MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , allowing compatible development workflows to use Floot's managed application infrastructure.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Codebase-wide understanding for smart edits
- Inline AI-assisted code editing and debugging
- Git integration with existing workflows
- Support for multiple programming languages
- VS Code-like interface for code-based development


### **Considerations**


Cursor is primarily designed for users comfortable working in a code editor, although its AI features can assist less experienced builders. Teams can configure deployment infrastructure separately or connect supported Cursor workflows to Floot.


Cursor has a free tier. Its newer subscription structure starts at $8/month for Plus, while Premium costs $30/month and supports additional development capabilities and third-party models billed separately. The former $20/month Pro plan is a legacy subscription.


## **7. Shipper**


Shipper combines app building with business strategy guidance. It generates product, design, and logic while also providing go-to-market planning.


### **Primary Focus**


Shipper positions itself as building like a co-founder rather than just a code generator. The platform includes monetization guidance for subscriptions and payments alongside the technical build.


This approach is relevant to founders developing an early product concept who want assistance with both application creation and the business decisions involved in preparing for launch.


### **Organizational Fit**


Shipper provides proactive AI suggestions, business strategy guidance, technical concept explanations for non-technical users, full-stack app generation, and monetization integration support.


Its combination of app development and business-oriented assistance may suit founders who want to evaluate product decisions during the building process.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Proactive AI suggesting improvements and opportunities
- Business strategy and go-to-market guidance
- Technical concept explanations for non-technical users
- Full-stack app generation
- Monetization integration support


### **Considerations**


Shipper's business-focused approach suits founders validating product ideas. Teams with established product direction may find the strategic features less relevant.


The Pro plan starts at $25 per user/month, billed monthly, with 100 credits per month.


## **8. FlutterFlow**


FlutterFlow is a visual Flutter app builder that generates Dart code, with full source-code export available on paid plans. It is designed specifically for mobile app development.


### **Primary Focus**


FlutterFlow produces Flutter applications that compile to native iOS and Android code. This distinguishes it from platforms that wrap web apps in mobile shells.


Its visual development environment allows teams to design interfaces, configure application behavior, and connect backend services while generating Flutter code for deployment.


### **Organizational Fit**


FlutterFlow offers native iOS and Android deployment, full source-code export on paid plans, Firebase integration for backend services, 1,000+ pre-built templates, and Figma-related design capabilities on eligible plans.


This workflow suits teams interested in visual app development while retaining the option to work with generated Flutter code.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Native iOS and Android deployment to app stores
- Full source-code export on paid plans
- Firebase integration for backend services
- 1,000+ pre-built templates
- Figma design integration on eligible plans


### **Considerations**


FlutterFlow's visual approach has a learning curve for complex logic. Teams comfortable with Flutter or willing to learn may value its native output for performance-sensitive[mobile applications](https://floot.com/blog/ai-app-builders-mobile-apps) .


Pricing starts at $39/month for the Basic plan under monthly billing.


## **9. Bubble**


Bubble is an established visual no-code platform with an AI Agent for application development. Bubble has reported that more than 7 million apps have been built on its platform across over 220 countries and territories.


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble offers a broad feature set for visual no-code development. Its plugin marketplace and visual workflow builder support application logic without requiring traditional programming.


The platform combines interface design, backend workflows, database management, and hosting within its visual development environment, making it suitable for teams that prefer configuring application behavior directly.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble provides visual programming with AI-assisted development, native iOS and Android app support, a large plugin marketplace, managed infrastructure, and workflows that remain visible and editable.


These capabilities support teams building applications through visual configuration rather than managing a conventional source-code development environment.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Visual programming with AI-assisted builds
- Native iOS and Android app support
- Large plugin marketplace
- Built-in security and managed hosting infrastructure
- Visible and editable application workflows


### **Considerations**


Bubble does not offer source-code export for its applications, creating a portability consideration for teams that may want to move to another development stack.


Pricing starts at $39/month for web applications, while combined web and mobile plans start at $69/month under monthly billing.


## **10. Joylo**


Joylo offers a written production guarantee for assessed and agreed project scopes when customers purchase the recommended engineering hours. Its optional Expert Assist service provides access to engineers with a 24-hour first-response commitment.


### **Primary Focus**


Joylo addresses the gap between AI-generated code and production-ready applications by pairing AI development with optional human engineering support.


The platform uses React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL on a portable stack, giving teams an approach that combines AI-assisted creation with engineering assistance for deployment and production issues.


### **Organizational Fit**


Joylo provides a written production guarantee for qualifying agreed scopes, AI Confidence Score assessments, GitHub-based code workflows, Expert Assist engineering support, and security review capabilities.


Its engineering service is particularly relevant to organizations that want additional human review before releasing applications to real users.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Written production guarantee for agreed scopes after purchasing recommended engineering hours
- AI Confidence Score auditing builds across five domains
- Code delivered to the customer's own GitHub
- Expert Assist connecting customers with engineers
- Security review support for production deployment


### **Considerations**


Joylo's Expert Assist model suits teams without in-house developers who still need engineering support for production deployment.


The human support layer is a paid service. Expert Assist starts at $500 for 10 engineering hours, with its 24-hour commitment referring to the first response rather than guaranteed project completion.


## **11. Emergent**


Emergent uses a multi-agent system to build both web and mobile apps. It is an option for teams looking to develop AI-generated applications with Python-based backends.


### **Primary Focus**


Emergent generates React and Next.js frontends with FastAPI backends and MongoDB databases. Its mobile development capabilities support applications targeting both web and mobile environments.


The platform's multi-agent approach separates development activities across tasks such as design, implementation, and testing, helping teams coordinate different parts of application creation.


### **Organizational Fit**


Emergent provides support for web and mobile development, Python-based backend functionality, multi-agent workflows, Expo-related mobile capabilities, and GitHub code export.


Teams comfortable with Python or interested in multi-agent app development may find this approach relevant to their project requirements.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Web and mobile application development
- Python backend via FastAPI
- Multi-agent workflows for development tasks
- Mobile development through Expo-related workflows
- GitHub code export


### **Considerations**


Teams comfortable with Python may prefer Emergent's backend approach over JavaScript-based alternatives. Its architecture and deployment services should be evaluated against application complexity, infrastructure requirements, and ongoing costs.


The Standard plan starts at $20/month when billed annually. Monthly billing and additional usage may cost more.


## **12. Base44**


Base44 is a managed no-code builder acquired by Wix in June 2025 for initial consideration of approximately $80 million, plus contingent earnout payments. It emphasizes simplicity with integrated backend services.


### **Primary Focus**


Base44 handles database, authentication, and hosting within the platform. As a Wix-owned product, Base44 offers managed infrastructure for teams prioritizing an integrated building and hosting experience.


Its conversational interface allows users to describe applications and refine functionality through AI-assisted development without configuring a separate backend for common workflows.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 provides integrated database, authentication, and hosting services, React and Vite-based applications using the Base44 SDK, GitHub synchronization on eligible plans, and a free monthly message-credit allocation.


Teams comparing managed development environments can explore[Base44 alternatives](https://floot.com/blog/base44-alternatives) to understand differences in infrastructure, code portability, and AI usage.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Integrated database, authentication, and hosting
- React and Vite codebase with Base44 SDK
- Two-way GitHub sync on Builder and higher plans
- Managed infrastructure within the Base44 platform
- 25 free message credits per month


### **Considerations**


GitHub synchronization requires the Builder plan at $50/month under monthly billing. Teams needing repository synchronization or source-code access on lower tiers should compare available export options.


Starter pricing begins at $20/month, while the Free plan includes limited monthly message and integration credits.


## **13. Claude Code**


Claude Code is Anthropic's conversational coding assistant with large context windows for multi-file understanding. It is particularly useful for reasoning through complex code changes.


### **Primary Focus**


Claude Code works alongside existing editors and Git workflows rather than replacing them. This makes it valuable for extending prototypes with complex backend logic, API integrations, and data processing.


Its coding workflows support developers working with established projects as well as teams creating new applications through AI-assisted programming.


### **Organizational Fit**


Claude Code supports project-wide refactoring, multi-file code understanding, backend and API development, and integration with existing development workflows.


It can also work with Floot's[managed app infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) through supported MCP configurations, allowing development tools and hosting services to complement one another.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Project-wide refactors from plain English
- Large context windows for multi-file understanding
- Backend, API, and data task handling
- Integration with existing development workflows
- Higher usage allowances on eligible Max plans


### **Considerations**


Claude Code is a coding assistant rather than a standalone managed app-hosting platform. Teams need deployment infrastructure, which they can configure separately or access through a platform such as Floot.


Claude Code is available through eligible Claude subscriptions or usage-billed API access. Infrastructure costs are separate from AI subscription or API charges.


## **14. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight applications directly inside ChatGPT. It supports persistent databases, file storage, sign-in features, and integrations with connected apps.


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites offers a direct path from a conversation to a published web experience without switching to a separate builder.


It suits dashboards, internal tools, resource hubs, and lightweight applications that fit its supported hosting environment. Users can build through conversation, review a private preview, and publish according to their plan and workspace permissions.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites provides website and lightweight app creation, persistent data storage, configurable sharing options, sign-in capabilities, and support for integrations with connected applications.


These capabilities suit eligible ChatGPT users who want to create and share interactive web experiences within the platform's supported runtime.


### **Production-Relevant Capabilities**


- Website and lightweight app generation inside ChatGPT
- Persistent databases and file storage
- Public and private publishing options
- Sign-in features and visitor access controls
- Integration with supported connected apps


### **Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites is available on eligible paid ChatGPT plans, with building and editing counted toward Codex usage. Hosting, storage, and runtime limitations depend on the applicable plan and workspace.


Teams should check supported frameworks, database constraints, hosting limits, and integration capabilities before choosing it for more complex applications.


For projects requiring managed Postgres infrastructure, authentication, payments, and mobile app publishing, Floot offers a separate[full-stack infrastructure workflow](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) that can work alongside compatible ChatGPT configurations.


## **Moving from Prototype to Production with Floot**


Floot helps non-technical founders, operators, and business owners turn AI-generated prototypes into working applications through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) . Supported assistants handle development tasks within their connector permissions, while Floot provides the infrastructure needed to host and maintain the app.


Its production-focused capabilities include:


- **Managed infrastructure:** Postgres databases, authentication, storage, email, backend endpoints, and hosting.
- **Mobile publishing:** iOS and Android builds without requiring local Xcode or Android Studio installations.
- **Code ownership:** Ownership of application code and data, with database exports on every plan and ZIP downloads on paid plans.
- **Flexible billing:** Daily building actions, separate optional AI credits, and usage-based hosting allowances.
- **Deployment support:** Live URLs, custom domains on eligible plans, and integrations for business applications.


Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , with paid plans offering higher building allowances and additional infrastructure capacity. Teams can continue using compatible AI assistants while managing application hosting, deployment, and ongoing development through Floot.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the core difference between MCP-connected AI app builders and platforms with their own agents?**


Platforms with their own AI agents may meter usage through subscriptions, message credits, or token allowances. MCP-connected platforms use an external AI assistant to carry out development tasks. Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) supports Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, subject to client permissions. Standard connector-based building uses daily building actions rather than Floot AI credits. Optional AI features, infrastructure usage, and the connected assistant's subscription remain separate cost considerations.


### **Can AI app builders create both web and mobile applications?**


Yes, but mobile deployment approaches differ. FlutterFlow generates Flutter applications, Expo supports React Native development, and other platforms package web apps in native shells. Floot's[mobile app workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) converts web applications into installable iOS and Android apps. Free includes 2 monthly builds, Pro includes 12, and Power offers unlimited builds. Publishing requires appropriate developer accounts. Apple Developer Program membership costs $99/year, while Google Play registration requires a $25 one-time fee. Store approval is not guaranteed.


### **What backend infrastructure do AI app builders need for production applications?**


Production applications commonly need databases, authentication, backend logic, file storage, and hosting. Some platforms provide these services directly, while others depend on external integrations. Floot includes managed Postgres databases, authentication, storage, and serverless endpoints. Its infrastructure supports applications with customer accounts, saved records, and business workflows. Teams should still evaluate database performance, backup options, hosting allowances, access permissions, and security requirements before launching applications for real users.


### **Are there AI app builders that are free to start, and what costs should users expect?**


Yes. Many platforms have free starting tiers with limits on messages, building actions, deployment features, or hosting usage. Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) include Free at $0/month, Pro at $25/month, and Power at $100/month. Free provides 100 daily building actions, 3,000 starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting allowance. Pro and Power offer higher daily actions, recurring hosting allowances, and monthly AI credits. Additional hosting usage and optional AI features can incur separate charges.


### **What should teams check for code ownership, data portability, and SEO?**


Code ownership, export access, and independent deployment capabilities are separate considerations. Teams should verify whether they can download application files, export database records, and run the generated code outside the original platform. For SEO, public-facing apps should support crawlable content, page metadata, canonical URLs, and sitemap configuration. Floot provides code and data ownership, paid project ZIP exports, and SEO functionality including pre-rendering and sitemap controls. Teams should validate these capabilities against their application's deployment and discoverability requirements before launch.
